**What type of PR is this?**

/kind cleanup


**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Based on the discussion in #87702 and #87783, Prefilter will always be invoked before Filter, so state should be computed and wrote to CycleState by Prefilter, it won't be nil now.
 
This PR does two things:
- return an error if expected states don't exist in CycleState
- remove the "slow-path" logic which was used to handle nil state case

issue_context.title: Cleanup "slow-path" logic in scheduler Filters
issue_context.body:
by "slow-paths"  we mean logic that allows executing Filters in the absence of PreFilter state. 

In the scheduler, it is not possible that a Filter will be invoked without invoking its PreFilter first, but we still have logic in Filters to allow this because historically ClusterAutoscaler didn't consistently call "MetadataProducer", neither kubelet and daemonset controller.

Now that both Kubelet and DaemonSet controller dependencies have been removed, and according to  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/87702#issuecomment-581298101, CA is consistently calling PreFilter, this special logic can be removed.


[ ] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/845b23232125caeb67eb30659ff482404a3d3735/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/filtering.go#L574

[ ] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/845b23232125caeb67eb30659ff482404a3d3735/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/filtering.go#L411

[ ] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/845b23232125caeb67eb30659ff482404a3d3735/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodeports/node_ports.go#L111

[ ] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/845b23232125caeb67eb30659ff482404a3d3735/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/noderesources/fit.go#L158

/sig scheduling
/help
/cc @losipiuk @MaciekPytel @Huang-Wei
comments:
ahg-g@ Just one note here; which I rose in the past. There is a possibility that we will need to add some optimization for features like pod inter-(anti)affinity. For which prefiltering is costly to compute; and yet often not needed. If we never reach the filter which checks pod-inter-affinity, because pod does not fit on node because of lack of resources, whole pre-filtering computation is a waste of time. 

We still need to do scalability testing with pod inter-(anti)affinity to see how big a problem is (if at all).

So with that in mind maybe it is worth to postpone pursuing with this effort a bit.

cc: @MaciekPytel

@losipiuk one solution is for CA to split the execution of filters into two phases: cheap and expensive filters. You can create two instances of the framework one for each phase:

```
cheapFwk, err := framework.NewFramework(
	plugins.NewInTreeRegistry(),
	cheapPlugins,
	cheapPluginConfigs,
        ...        
)

expensiveFwk, err := framework.NewFramework(
	plugins.NewInTreeRegistry(),
	expensivePlugins,
	expensivePluginConfigs,
        ...        
)

cheapFwk.RunPreFilter()
s := cheapFwk.RunFilter(node)

if s == Success {
  expensiveFwk.RunPreFilter()
  s = expensiveFwk.RunFilter(node)
}


```

Yeah - I guess that would work. The only problem I see with that is that we need to be aware of the list of plugins. And not just depend on what is in default registry. But I guess we can live with that. Let's see what tests show. And implement that only if needed.
We could have those two sets as two separate providers in the scheduler, and the default one is always the combination of the two.
@ahg-g shoud we return an error if the state is nil, or just remove the else branch?

> We could have those two sets as two separate providers in the scheduler, and the default one is always the combination of the two.

This seems kinda CA specific. But if you are fine to maintain such two sets it would be great. Then source of truth, what is the set of plugins, would live in single repo.

There is a similar logic in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d0f582c9bf83d67b41020600f293e11a7f322d01/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/serviceaffinity/service_affinity.go#L250

Do we need to clean this one?

yes, we need to clean this up as well.

For each filter that expects prefilter state, we should return an error if it didn't exist in CycleState.

Great. I created https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/87822 to track this. And assigned to @aleksandra-malinowska to verify if we need it.

review_comments: We should keep this test and verify that an error is returned when invoking Filter without calling PreFilter. The unit test should be simple.
keep the test and verify that Filter returns error.
Keep the test and verify that Filter now returns an error (it should be a single test case).

The weight here is confusing, in a followup PR I suggest we change ```RegisterPluginAsExtensions``` to not set the weight, and have another function ```RegisterPluginAsExtensionsWithWeight``` that accept a weight parameter for the extensions that require a weight.
I'll send another PR for this.
